message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"8.24","text":"When he had said these things, everyone remained—some for the sake of being healed, and others in order to observe those who obtained healing. Peter merely laid his hands on them and prayed, and he healed them, so that those who had been healed at once became overjoyed, while those who had observed were extraordinarily amazed and, after praising God, believed with assured hope. Together with those who had been healed, they went away to their own homes under instructions to gather early the next day. After they had left, Peter remained there with his companions, partook of food, and gave himself rest in sleep.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τοῦ ἱστορῆσαι τοὺς τῆς θεραπείας ἐπιτυγχάνοντας","chosen":"in order to observe those who obtained healing","rationale":"ἱστορέω can mean to inquire into or observe closely; remaining at the scene to witness the healings supports “observe.”"},{"source_quote":"τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῖς ἐπιθεὶς μόνον καὶ εὐξάμενος ἰάσατο","chosen":"merely laid his hands on them and prayed, and he healed them","rationale":"μόνον emphasizes the simplicity of Peter’s actions accompanying the healing."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς μὲν παραχρῆμα θεραπευθέντας γενέσθαι περιχαρεῖς","chosen":"those who had been healed at once became overjoyed","rationale":"The placement of παραχρῆμα within the participial phrase marks the healing as immediate rather than the subsequent becoming overjoyed."},{"source_quote":"βεβαίας ἐλπίδος πιστεύειν","chosen":"believed with assured hope","rationale":"The genitive phrase is taken as characterizing the hope accompanying their belief; “believed in a sure hope” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"πρωΐτερον τῇ ὑστεραίᾳ συνελθεῖν","chosen":"to gather early the next day","rationale":"Although πρωΐτερον is morphologically comparative, it is taken here in an absolute or elative sense, referring to an early time. The formally comparative alternative is “to gather earlier the next day,” with the point of comparison left implicit."},{"source_quote":"διανέπαυσεν ἑαυτὸν τῷ ὕπνῳ","chosen":"gave himself rest in sleep","rationale":"Preserves both the reflexive expression and the explicit reference to sleep rather than reducing the phrase simply to “slept.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"βεβαίας ἐλπίδος πιστεύειν","issue":"The genitive βεβαίας ἐλπίδος has more than one defensible relation to πιστεύειν. The translation takes it as characterizing the hope accompanying their belief; an alternative is “believed in a sure hope.” The construction remains intelligible without conjecture.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"πρωΐτερον τῇ ὑστεραίᾳ συνελθεῖν","issue":"πρωΐτερον is comparative in form. The translation understands it absolutely or elatively as “early,” while “to gather earlier the next day,” with an implicit comparison point, is also defensible. This is an interpretive ambiguity, not evidence of source corruption.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
